decisions.reason: Define-XML ADLBC.AVISIT enumerates visit labels but no period value; both reported outputs contain a nonblank period string. Trimming its storage padding does not make it a listed code or a missing character value.

Retained Define-XML ADLBC.A1LO._ALB through ._URATE (beginning at line 7825) explicitly says 'Set to missing', while ordinary parameter ItemDefs copy LB.LBSTNRLO. The reported differences are on the change-parameter records governed by that missing-value rule, so the variable-level copy comparison applies the wrong rule to those records.

Retained Define-XML ADLBC.A1HI._ALB through ._URATE (beginning at line 7519) explicitly says 'Set to missing', while ordinary parameter ItemDefs copy LB.LBSTNRHI. The reported differences are on the change-parameter records governed by that missing-value rule, so the variable-level copy comparison applies the wrong rule to those records.

Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1LO divides by A1HI, the opposite normal limit from the lower-limit ratio named by its label and SAP page 12. These are different denominators, not alternative wording of the same ratio.

The helpers feeding adlbc-probe.yaml lines 242-255 apply the Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1LO formula AVAL/A1HI and its stated precision to published upstream values. The reported differences follow that rule, and the SAP page 12 limit reading still differs after the same precision is applied.

Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1HI divides by A1LO, the opposite normal limit from the upper-limit ratio named by its label and SAP page 12. These are different denominators, not alternative wording of the same ratio.

The helpers feeding adlbc-probe.yaml lines 264-277 apply the Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1HI formula AVAL/A1LO and its stated precision to published upstream values. The reported differences follow that rule, and the SAP page 12 limit reading still differs after the same precision is applied.
Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1LO states AVAL/A1HI at baseline, while the variable label and SAP page 12 identify the lower-limit ratio. The baseline qualifier does not reconcile the opposite denominator.

The _LBC2_BL lookup in adlbc-probe.yaml selects the published baseline-flagged record within subject and parameter before lines 286-299 calculate AVAL/A1HI with the stated precision. This preserves Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1LO's baseline qualifier; both the literal and SAP-limit results differ as reported.
Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1HI states AVAL/A1LO at baseline, while the variable label and SAP page 12 identify the upper-limit ratio. The baseline qualifier does not reconcile the opposite denominator.

The _LBC2_BL lookup in adlbc-probe.yaml selects the published baseline-flagged record within subject and parameter before lines 308-321 calculate AVAL/A1LO with the stated precision. This preserves Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1HI's baseline qualifier; both the literal and SAP-limit results differ as reported.

Define-XML ADLBC.ALBTRVAL states the maximum of result minus 1.5*ULN and 0.5*LLN minus result, with precision 3. The _LBC2_HIGH_EXCESS, _LBC2_LOW_EXCESS and _LBC2_THRESHOLD helpers feeding adlbc-probe.yaml lines 338-344 preserve both subtraction directions and use the matched raw LB normal limits, so the reported differences follow the literal rule.

SAP page 11 explicitly includes laboratory assessments in actual-date visit assignment. adlbc.yaml base-ord maps LB.VISIT labels directly and supplies no actual-date window counterpart in the other row rules or helpers.

Define-XML ADLBC.ADY names LB.LBDY, whereas adlbc.yaml lines 991-1005 calculate study_day from _ADT_DATE and TRTSDT. The row rules derive _ADT_DATE from LB.LBDTC and never read LB.LBDY, so this is a different source/computation even if values agree.

adlbc.yaml base-ord and under-ord explicitly copy LB.VISIT, and base-eot and under-eot retain LB.VISIT through ONLY on the selected source-record group. These row-rule derivations implement the source named by Define-XML ADLBC.VISIT; the empty column-level derivation is not a source difference.

adlbc.yaml base-ord and under-ord explicitly copy LB.VISITNUM, and base-eot and under-eot retain LB.VISITNUM through ONLY on the selected source-record group. These row-rule derivations implement the source named by Define-XML ADLBC.VISITNUM; the empty column-level derivation is not a source difference.

Define-XML ADLBC.PARAM requires the source LB.LBTEST and LB.LBSTRESU concatenation for ordinary parameters. adlbc.yaml base-ord instead maps LB.LBTESTCD to fixed text in _PARAM_BASE, and PARAM uses that text; no helper reads the specified test-name and unit sources for this computation.

adlbc.yaml row rules base-ord and base-eot read LB.LBSTNRLO directly or through ONLY, while under-ord and under-eot set A1LO missing. Those branches implement the ordinary-copy and change-parameter missingness stated in retained Define-XML ADLBC.A1LO value-level ItemDefs (including line 7825); a missing column-level derivation does not establish a source divergence.

adlbc.yaml row rules base-ord and base-eot read LB.LBSTNRHI directly or through ONLY, while under-ord and under-eot set A1HI missing. Those branches implement the ordinary-copy and change-parameter missingness stated in retained Define-XML ADLBC.A1HI value-level ItemDefs (including line 7519); a missing column-level derivation does not establish a source divergence.

Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1LO specifies AVAL/A1HI, whereas adlbc.yaml R2A1LO uses _AVAL_BASE/A1LO. For ordinary parameters _AVAL_BASE is the source value, but the denominator remains the opposite documented limit.

Define-XML ADLBC.R2A1HI specifies AVAL/A1LO, whereas adlbc.yaml R2A1HI uses _AVAL_BASE/A1HI. For ordinary parameters _AVAL_BASE is the source value, but the denominator remains the opposite documented limit.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1LO specifies AVAL/A1HI at baseline; adlbc.yaml BR2A1LO instead divides _BASE by the current row's A1LO. The _BASE helpers select the baseline numerator but do not restore the documented denominator or explicitly select the baseline-record limit.

Define-XML ADLBC.BR2A1HI specifies AVAL/A1LO at baseline; adlbc.yaml BR2A1HI instead divides _BASE by the current row's A1HI. The _BASE helpers select the baseline numerator but do not restore the documented denominator or explicitly select the baseline-record limit.
Define-XML ADLBC.ALBTRVAL specifies max(result-1.5*ULN, 0.5*LLN-result). adlbc.yaml base-ord instead takes the maximum of 1.5*A1HI-_AVAL_BASE and _AVAL_BASE-0.5*A1LO, reversing both subtractions.

Define-XML ADLBC.ALBTRVAL specifies max(result-1.5*ULN, 0.5*LLN-result). adlbc.yaml under-ord instead takes the maximum of 1.5*_B_A1HI-_AVAL_BASE and _AVAL_BASE-0.5*_B_A1LO, reversing both subtractions.

SAP page 17 and retained Define-XML ADLBC.ABLFL.ALB (line 7969) identify Visit 1, while adlbc.yaml base-ord tests LB.LBBLFL alone. The retained SDTM LBBLFL comment (define-sdtm.xml line 3511) says VISIT='SCREENING' and does not supply an exact Visit 1 condition for this branch.

Define-XML ADLBC.AENTMTFL distinguishes Visit 12 from a last assessment selected for discontinuation before Visit 12. adlbc.yaml AENTMTFL and its _IS_LAST_ELIGIBLE/_IS_EOT helpers flag the last eligible scheduled record and its derived row without testing that early-discontinuation condition.

SAP page 12 calls for the last observed on-treatment value, whereas adlbc.yaml base-ord orders eligible records by descending LBSEQ without an assessment-date ordering. Retained SDTM LB.LBSEQ (define-sdtm.xml line 3392) defines a sequential record identifier, not a guarantee of observation chronology.

SAP page 11 states both the general CRF-visit convention and additional actual-date laboratory assignment with nearest-target and earlier-assessment tie rules, but its window table names only ADAS-Cog/CIBIC+ and NPI-X. SAP page 17 supplies scheduled laboratory visits and baseline, with no laboratory window boundaries or target days, so a complete laboratory actual-date probe still needs an unstated window policy.

The report's stated obstacle is omission of those retained ItemDefs from the citable-section adapter, which does not establish incomplete source documentation under CR-10.

Define-XML ADLBC.AENTMTFL requires discontinuation before Visit 12, whereas ADSL.DISCONFL identifies study discontinuation and ADSL.VISNUMEN selects DS records with DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED', without specifying how either supplies that flag's early-discontinuation condition. SAP pages 10, 12, 17 and 34 provide end-of-treatment and phase descriptions but do not resolve that operational condition or identify study discontinuation with discontinuation of study drug.

SAP page 11 includes laboratory assessments in the paragraph requiring selection of the assessment closest to the target day within a visit window. The AVISIT branches in base-ord/under-ord and the end-of-treatment row rules use visit labels and LBSEQ ranking, with no nearest-target selection counterpart.

SAP page 11 requires the assessment before the target day when two assessments are equidistant, in the same paragraph that includes laboratory assessments. No AVISIT branch or other rule in adlbc.yaml compares distances from a target day or applies this tie rule.
